issues.description: Email regex is overly permissive and allows invalid email formats (e.g., 'user@domain' without TLD, multiple @ symbols in local part)
issues.suggestion: Use a more robust email validation regex or a dedicated validation library like validator.js. Consider: /^[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*$/

issues.description: HTML entity encoding is incomplete for XSS prevention. Missing encoding for other dangerous characters like forward slash (/) which can break out of some contexts
issues.suggestion: Use a well-tested sanitization library like DOMPurify or the OWASP Java Encoder equivalent for JavaScript. If manual encoding is required, also encode: &, /, and consider the specific context (HTML, attribute, JavaScript, CSS, URL)

issues.description: Sanitization function doesn't handle null/undefined inputs, which could cause runtime errors
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: 'export function sanitizeInput(input: string): string { if (!input) return ''; // ... rest of code }'

issues.description: ID generation uses weak randomness (Math.random()) and predictable timestamp, making IDs guessable and potentially exploitable for enumeration attacks
issues.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID() for secure random IDs: 'import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'; function generateId(): string { return randomUUID(); }' or use a library like uuid with v4 UUIDs

issues.description: ID generation has collision risk in high-concurrency scenarios due to reliance on Date.now() and weak randomness
issues.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID() or a proven ID generation library like nanoid or uuid to ensure uniqueness even under high load

issues.description: Error messages expose internal implementation details that could aid attackers in reconnaissance
issues.suggestion: Use generic user-facing error messages and log detailed errors separately. Consider: 'throw new Error('Invalid input provided')' and log specific validation failures server-side

issues.description: Email is not sanitized before storage, though toLowerCase() provides basic normalization. Consider additional validation for disposable/temporary email services if business logic requires
issues.suggestion: If needed, add additional email validation to block disposable email services or validate MX records for the domain

issues.description: Database query is commented out, making the code incomplete for production use. No error handling for database operations
issues.suggestion: Implement actual database connection with proper error handling: wrap in try-catch, handle connection failures, deadlocks, and constraint violations appropriately

issues.description: Input validation checks for falsy values, but empty strings would pass the truthy check. Explicit empty string validation would be more robust
issues.suggestion: Use more explicit validation: 'if (!input.email?.trim() || !input.name?.trim()) { throw new Error('Email and name are required'); }'

issues.description: No maximum length validation on input fields, which could allow excessive data storage or buffer issues
issues.suggestion: Add length validation: 'if (input.name.length > 255 || input.email.length > 255) { throw new Error('Input exceeds maximum length'); }'

codeQuality.summary: This code demonstrates good security awareness with input validation, sanitization, and parameterized queries. However, several medium-severity issues were identified: (1) weak email validation regex that allows invalid formats, (2) incomplete XSS sanitization missing key characters, and (3) cryptographically weak ID generation using Math.random() that could enable enumeration attacks. The code also has minor gaps in error handling, edge case validation (null/empty strings), and length limits. To achieve production-ready quality, replace manual validation/sanitization with proven libraries (validator.js, DOMPurify), use crypto.randomUUID() for secure IDs, add comprehensive input validation including length limits, and implement proper database error handling. Overall, this is decent foundation code that needs hardening before production deployment.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email validation is a security-critical function that guards user input. Invalid regex patterns or edge cases could allow malformed emails into the system, leading to downstream failures or security vulnerabilities.

Test: 'should reject email without domain extension' - Input: isValidEmail('user@gmail') - Expected: false. Test: 'should accept valid email' - Input: isValidEmail('user@example.com') - Expected: true. Test: 'should reject email with spaces' - Input: isValidEmail('user @example.com') - Expected: false.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email validation must handle empty strings, special characters, and internationalized domains. Missing edge case handling could allow invalid data or reject valid international emails.

Test: 'should reject null-like strings' - Input: isValidEmail('null') where input is empty after trim - Expected: false. Test: 'should handle multiple @ symbols' - Input: isValidEmail('user@@example.com') - Expected: false. Test: 'should handle consecutive dots' - Input: isValidEmail('user@example..com') - Expected: false.

Test: 'should escape double quotes' - Input: sanitizeInput('Hello "World"') - Expected: 'Hello "World"'. Test: 'should escape single quotes' - Input: sanitizeInput("It's here") - Expected: 'It's here'.

Test: 'should handle already escaped content' - Input: sanitizeInput('<tag>') - Expected: '&lt;tag&gt;' (or document if double-escaping is intentional). Test: 'should handle strings with only special characters' - Input: sanitizeInput('<>"\'\'"<>') - Expected: '<>"''"<>'.

testCoverage.summary: The file fixtures/clean-code.ts has NO test coverage (0%). No test files were found for this module. This is a security-critical module containing email validation, XSS sanitization, and user creation logic. CRITICAL gaps include: (1) isValidEmail function lacks tests for valid/invalid email formats and edge cases like empty strings, multiple @ symbols, and special characters. (2) sanitizeInput function has no tests verifying XSS prevention for <, >, quotes, or edge cases like empty strings and Unicode. (3) createUser function lacks tests for the happy path, all error branches (missing email/name, invalid format), and integration with sanitization and persistence. (4) generateId lacks uniqueness and format validation tests. (5) saveUser has no tests for parameter handling or error scenarios. HIGH-PRIORITY recommendations: (a) Add comprehensive tests for isValidEmail covering 10+ valid and invalid email patterns. (b) Add XSS sanitization tests with actual attack vectors. (c) Add end-to-end createUser tests mocking saveUser to verify complete workflows. (d) Add error handling tests for all validation branches. (e) Add edge case tests for database failures, concurrent access, and Unicode handling. The module appears to follow security best practices in code, but without tests, regressions could easily be introduced.

refactorings.summary: This is well-structured code with good practices already in place. The identified refactoring opportunities are primarily focused on: (1) modernizing ID generation with crypto.randomUUID() for better uniqueness guarantees, (2) extracting validation and user building logic into separate functions for better separation of concerns and testability, (3) creating custom error classes for more precise error handling, (4) improving the HTML sanitization with a more maintainable data-driven approach, and (5) adding proper dependency injection for the database client. All suggestions are low-to-medium impact improvements that would enhance maintainability, testability, and robustness without changing core functionality. The code demonstrates good security practices (parameterized queries, input sanitization) and async/await patterns.

recommendations.description: Add comprehensive test coverage for security-critical functions. The file has 0% test coverage with 16 untested paths. Priority should be given to testing email validation (isValidEmail), XSS sanitization (sanitizeInput), and the main business logic (createUser) including all error branches.

Replace weak ID generation (Math.random() + timestamp) with crypto.randomUUID() to prevent enumeration attacks and ID collisions in high-concurrency scenarios. Current implementation is predictable and exploitable.

Enhance XSS sanitization to include all dangerous characters (ampersand, forward slash) and consider using a proven library like DOMPurify instead of manual encoding. Current implementation is incomplete.
Improve email validation regex to reject invalid formats (missing TLD, multiple @ symbols, etc.) or use a dedicated validation library like validator.js. Current regex is overly permissive.

Extract validation logic into separate functions (validateCreateUserInput, buildUser) to improve separation of concerns, testability, and maintainability. This follows the Single Responsibility Principle.
Implement custom error classes (e.g., ValidationError) for better error differentiation and type safety. This will make error handling more robust and provide better context to consumers.
Add input validation for edge cases: null/undefined handling in sanitizeInput, empty string checks with .trim(), and maximum length validation for email and name fields to prevent buffer issues.
Implement database dependency injection with proper typing (DatabaseClient interface) to make the code more testable and production-ready. Currently the database query is commented out.
